newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies higher.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while pork belly futures were expected to open 0.250 to 1.000 higher, livestock analysts said.

Spillover strength from pork belly futures is likely in hog futures early but weakness in cash hog prices will likely weigh on live hog futures. Rain moving through the Midwest has taken farmers from fieldwork and allowed them more time to market hogs, analysts said.
Higher pork cutout values with a firmer loin market may also lend support, they said.

Pork bellies were seen higher following the bullishly construed weekly CME out-of-town storage report. The CME reported a net out-movement last week of 1.205 million lbs, exceeding analysts' estimates of in movement of 200,000 lbs to out movement of 200,000 lbs.
Most analysts viewed the unexpected large out-movement as confirmation of increased export business or movement of product to non-reporting warehouses for later export.
However, gains in futures will likely be tempered by easier cash belly prices which ranged lower on Tuesday, sources noted.
